AIM:

The objective of the tool is to evaluate the climate risk and vulnerability of communities. The tool assesses how current climate hazards (such as temperature, Precipitation, droughts and floods) impact the broader community. Based on the prevailing risk and vulnerability, the tool explores potential interventions that will improve climate resilience.
This tool is focused on assessing the current risk and vulnerability levels for communities. In addition to the assets lens, gender, green infrastructure and the socio-ecological benefits that it provides, is also explored.
The tool also uses the updated Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) methodology, as discussed in detail in the section below.
FRAMEWORK:
In line with the Fifth Assessment Report (AR5) by the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC), the tool includes the following aspects:

r.t: the occurrence or potential occurrence of a climate-related event (such as rainfall or temperature) and/or a natural or human-induced impact (such as flood or droughts), that has or may cause harm, injury, damage or the loss of a system, species or asset.
the degree to which a system, species or asset is ‘exposed’, due to its location or presence in a place or setting that is or could be impacted by a climate-related hazard.
the susceptibility of a system, species or asset to climate-related impacts, or the degree to which system, species or asset is or can be directly or indirectly impacted by a climate-related hazard.

the proven or perceived ability of a system, species or asset to respond to existing or potential climate-related impacts and adjust to damage, so as to cope with consequences and take advantage of opportunities.
the inclination of a system, species or asset to be impacted by climate-related hazards, encompassing its sensitivity and its ability to cope or adapt to climate-related impacts.
refers to the potential for (and the likelihood of) adverse climate-related impacts on a system, species or asset, resulting from the interaction of vulnerability, exposure, and hazard.

si.t: The tool relies on several questions that assess hazard, exposure, sensitivity and adaptive capacity. As shown above, the responses to these categories, will enable an assessment of risk and vulnerability will be assessed. Based on the prevalent risk and vulnerability, the tool explores potential response measures that will improve climate resilience by either decreasing sensitivity or increasing adaptive capacity. In addition, whenever possible, measures to decrease exposure will be explored.
HOW TO USE THIS TOOL:

The grey rectangular boxes enable the user to explore through the tool. The boxes will either lead the user to a different place in the same rectanglar tab, or to a new rectanglar tab. Therefore, please click on any grey box to navigate and to complete the tool.
The user is required to answer the questions provided under the "Hazard" rectanglar tab, "Exposure" rectanglar tab, "Sensitivity" rectanglar tab, as well as the "Adaptive Capacity" rectanglar tab. The user can access these rectanglar tabs by clicking on the "Hazard", "Exposure", "Sensitivity", and the "Adaptive Capacity" boxes. In these rectanglar tabs, questions are provided for "Hazard", "Exposure", "Sensitivity", and "Adaptive Capacity".
The "Output" rectanglar tab leads the user to the "RVAT" rectanglar tab, where the answer to each question are analysed using the framework, assessed and graphed. Specifically, the tool provides outputs for "Vulnerability" and "Risk". Based on the “Risk” output, which incorporates “vulnerability”, the tool provides response options. These can be accessed by clicking on the "Responses" rectanglar tab at the top of your screen, or by clicking the "Responses" rectanglar tab.
